phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence: Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON
[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: ERROR:UNKNOWN:SON)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

→ Device state: ON (armed) — response: SWITCH:on
ACK
